Covers the national territory including the offshore cays. Wikipedia's Belize article rounds to 22,966.

languages.note: English is the sole official language; Belizean Creole, Spanish and Mayan languages are widely spoken but not official (ownerRules: languages English).

funFact.value: Belize's capital, Belmopan, was built inland after Hurricane Hattie devastated the old capital, Belize City, in 1961.
funFact.note: 117 characters. Wikipedia: Belmopan became the capital after Hurricane Hattie's 1961 devastation of Belize City; the planned city lies about 80 km inland.

driveSide.note: Matches the seed (leftHand false). The raw Wikipedia traffic table lists Belize as RHT, switched in 1961 to match its neighbours while still a British colony.

flag.text: The flag grew from the blue and white banner of the People's United Party, founded in 1950 to lead the push for independence; the ring of 50 leaves recalls that year. Red stripes were added in 1981 for the rival United Democratic Party. The coat of arms honors the timber trade: a mahogany tree, logging tools, a ship, and two woodcutters, one mestizo with an axe and one Afro-Belizean with a paddle. The motto means Under the shade I flourish.

reasons.feature: Blue background with the coat of arms on a white disc
reasons.why: This was the flag of the People's United Party (PUP), the party that led the independence movement from 1950; blue is the PUP's color. The national flag adopted on 21 September 1981 kept it.

reasons.feature: Red stripes along the top and bottom
reasons.why: Added when the flag was adopted at independence on 21 September 1981 so that the color of the opposition United Democratic Party (UDP, founded 1973) was included; Wikipedia: the red stripes were added to denote the colour of the opposition party.

reasons.feature: Wreath of 50 leaves around the arms
reasons.why: The 50 leaves recall the year 1950, when the PUP was founded and organized opposition to British rule began; Wikipedia's flag article phrases it as the year the PUP came to power.

reasons.feature: Two men holding the shield (left, lighter-skinned, with an axe; right, darker-skinned, with a paddle)
reasons.why: They are the supporters of the colonial coat of arms (granted 1907, with roots in an 1819 design) and represent the woodcutters of the mahogany trade: one mestizo and one man of African descent; the axe felled trees and the paddle moved logs by river. Britannica notes both figures were originally of African descent and the design later changed to one mestizo and one Afro-descendant man. In the flag image the left man carries the axe and the right man the paddle.
Mahogany logging was the basis of the colony's economy in the 18th and 19th centuries and the reason for British settlement; the tree stands for that forest wealth.

reasons.feature: Shield with a paddle and maul, a saw and axe, and a sailing ship
reasons.why: The tools are those of the timber industry and the ship stands for shipping the wood overseas, all from the colonial arms.

reasons.feature: Motto Sub Umbra Floreo on the scroll
reasons.why: Latin for Under the Shade I Flourish, a reference to the mahogany forests and, historically, to the settlement's growth under British protection.

reasons.feature: Meaning of the colors blue, red and white
reasons.why: Wikipedia's flag article gives no official meaning for the colors beyond the party origins (blue = PUP, red = UDP); no government color symbolism was read.

entries.remainingDoubts: The Belize government's National Symbols page (belize.gov.bz) returned HTTP 503 in the drafting pass, so the official wording for the 50 leaves and the two figures was not read from a government source; Wikipedia and Britannica agree on them. Wikipedia's flag article says the 50 leaves recall 1950 as the year the PUP came to power, Britannica frames 1950 as the PUP's founding year; the entry uses the founding. The flag article names a mestizo and a man of African descent but does not say which holds the axe and which the paddle; the assignment follows the flag image and the coat-of-arms description. Population is WPP 2024 as reproduced by Worldometers, not read from population.un.org directly. Currency sign BZ$ is the customary symbol; the page opened only gave the ISO code BZD.

driveSide.note: Matches the seed. Wikipedia's traffic table lists Costa Rica as RHT and the country infobox says driving side right.

flag.text: The blue and white bands come from the Central American federation of 1823, whose flag was modeled on Argentina's. In 1848 Pacífica Fernández, the president's wife, had a red band added in the center, inspired by the French flag in that year of revolution; the red was then said to stand for the civilization of the century. Blue is often read as the sky, white as peace and red as the warmth of the people. Everyday flags carry no coat of arms.

reasons.why: Costa Rica belonged to the Federal Republic of Central America (United Provinces) from 1823 and used its blue-white-blue flag, which took inspiration from Argentina's flag; this is the shared Central American blue-white-blue motif also seen on the flags of El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Guatemala.

reasons.feature: Wide red band in the center
reasons.why: Created on 29 September 1848 under President José María Castro Madriz at the suggestion of his wife Pacífica Fernández Oreamuno, an admirer of France, the scene of revolution in 1848. Spanish Wikipedia gives the instrument as Decree No. 147 of 29 September 1848; English Wikipedia gives the date but no decree number. The red was said at the time to represent the civilization of the century.

reasons.feature: Meaning of blue, white and red
reasons.why: Popular readings: blue for the sky, opportunity, idealism and perseverance; white for peace, wisdom and happiness; red for the warmth and generosity of the people and the blood shed for freedom. English Wikipedia lists these meanings without citing any law or official source; Law 18 of 1906 and the later color law set the design and shades.

reasons.feature: No coat of arms on the flag shown
reasons.why: The plain five-band flag is the civil flag used by citizens; the state flag, adopted 27 November 1906 and modified in 1998, carries the national coat of arms and is only permitted to be used by the government.

entries.remainingDoubts: No official Costa Rican government statement of color meanings was found; English Wikipedia gives the meanings without citing a law, so they are hedged as traditional. The decree number 147 comes from Spanish Wikipedia only. Area: the area list gives 51,180 km2 while 51,100 is the commonly cited figure. Population is WPP 2024 as reproduced by Worldometers, not read from population.un.org directly. The colón sign ₡ was not shown on the page opened (only the code CRC).

funFact.value: El Salvador is the only Central American country with no Caribbean coast; all of its shoreline faces the Pacific Ocean.
funFact.note: 119 characters. Wikipedia: El Salvador is the only Central American country lacking a Caribbean coastline.

driveSide.note: Matches the seed. Wikipedia's traffic table lists El Salvador as RHT with no notes.

flag.text: The bands copy the flag of the Central American federation of 1823 and were readopted in 1912. Blue is usually read as the two oceans around Central America, white as peace. The coat of arms, ringed by the country's name in gold, has five volcanoes for the federation's five states, a red liberty cap, a rainbow, the independence date 15 September 1821, five flags, 14 laurel bunches for the 14 departments, and the motto God, Union, Liberty.

reasons.why: Taken from the flag of the Federal Republic of Central America (United Provinces, 1823), which El Salvador belonged to; that flag was in turn inspired by Argentina's. This is the shared Central American blue-white-blue motif also used by Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala and Costa Rica.

reasons.feature: Adoption of the current design in 1912
reasons.why: The Legislative Assembly adopted the federation-style flag on 17 May 1912, replacing a stars-and-stripes style flag used from 1865 to 1912; the change reflected opposition to US interventions in Latin America at the time.

Blue is explained as the Pacific and Atlantic (Caribbean) waters that frame Central America and white as peace. Wikipedia attributes this to the 1972 Law of National Symbols, but the law text opened (Decreto 115) only describes the design in Article 5 and no article giving color meanings was found, so the meaning is treated as a widely repeated reading rather than confirmed statute text.

reasons.feature: Golden triangle with five volcanoes rising from two seas
reasons.why: The 1972 law prescribes a triangle holding a chain of five volcanoes on land bathed by two seas. The five volcanoes come from the 1823 federal arms and stand for the five member states of the Central American federation (Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica) between the Pacific and the Caribbean. The triangle is popularly read as equality or the three branches of government.

reasons.feature: Red liberty cap on a golden staff with rays and the date 15 DE SEPTIEMBRE DE 1821
reasons.why: The law prescribes the cap of liberty spreading light with the date written among its rays. The red cap (a Phrygian cap) is a long-standing symbol of freedom from republican tradition, and the date is Central America's declaration of independence from Spain on 15 September 1821.
Prescribed by the law, which gives no meaning for it; it is traditionally said to be a symbol of peace, often linked to the biblical rainbow after the flood.

reasons.feature: Five blue-and-white flags on spears behind the triangle
reasons.why: The flags are prescribed by law and are usually read as the five federation states again; Wikipedia adds that the spears are said to recall the country's Indigenous heritage, but no official meaning is given.

reasons.feature: Laurel wreath in 14 bunches tied with a blue and white ribbon
reasons.why: The 1972 law states that the wreath's bunches (gajos) equal the number of administrative departments of the Republic, which is 14; laurel traditionally stands for glory.

reasons.feature: Gold ring of text REPUBLICA DE EL SALVADOR EN LA AMERICA CENTRAL and the motto DIOS UNION LIBERTAD
reasons.why: Both inscriptions are prescribed by the 1972 law: the ring gives the country's name and places it in Central America, and the motto means God, Union, Liberty. The law also requires the motto on official documents.

entries.remainingDoubts: The 1972 Ley de Símbolos Patrios text extracted in the drafting pass describes the flag and arms in detail but no clause stating what the colors mean was found, although Wikipedia attributes the two-oceans/peace reading to that law; the color meaning is therefore labelled traditional. Meanings for the triangle, rainbow and five flags are popular readings, not statute. The El Salvador flag and arms claims were not re-fetched in the review pass (tool budget); the area figure was re-checked against the raw area list. Population is WPP 2024 as reproduced by Worldometers, not read from population.un.org directly. Wikipedia says the Salvadoran colón technically remains legal tender though out of circulation; the currency follows ownerRules (US Dollar only).

flag.text: The blue and white come from the flag of the Federal Republic of Central America. Guatemala restored them in 1871, with upright bands to differ from its neighbors, and added its arms. Officially, blue stands for strength, justice, truth and loyalty, and white for purity, integrity, firmness and light. The quetzal bird means freedom, the scroll gives the independence date, and rifles, swords and laurels mean defense, honor and victory.

reasons.why: Taken from the flag of the Federal Republic of Central America, which Guatemala belonged to after independence from Spain in 1821; Wikipedia: the federal flag was used until 1851, when a pro-Spanish faction took over and added the Spanish colors red and yellow, and the original colors were restored on 17 August 1871. Shared Central American blue-white-blue origin with El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica.
Wikipedia: the colors were restored in 1871 as vertical rather than horizontal stripes in order to distinguish the flag from other flags (the horizontal blue-white-blue flags of its neighbors).

The Flag of Guatemala article states that the two sky blue stripes represent strength, justice, truth and loyalty, and the white purity, integrity, firmness and light. No decree number or year is cited on the page (verified in the review pass), so the text says 'Officially' rather than naming a decree.

The national bird; the flag article says it symbolizes liberty. Per the Emblem article the coat of arms was adopted by Executive Decree No. 33 of 18 November 1871 under President Miguel García Granados, possibly designed by Swiss engraver Johann Baptist Frener (Emblem page not re-opened in the review pass).

reasons.feature: Scroll reading LIBERTAD 15 DE SEPTIEMBRE DE 1821
reasons.why: Records the date of Central American independence from Spain, 15 September 1821 (confirmed on the flag article). The 1997 spelling correction from SETIEMBRE to SEPTIEMBRE comes from the Emblem article per the draft and was not re-verified.
Flag article: indicate Guatemala's willingness to defend itself by force if need be; the Emblem article identifies them as Remington rifles, the type used in the 1871 Liberal Revolution.
Flag article: represent honor (the Emblem article adds justice).
Flag article: the symbol for victory. A 1968 decree standardizing the arms is mentioned in the Emblem article per the draft.

entries.remainingDoubts: Languages: only Spanish is official, but Guatemala's 2003 Law of National Languages recognizes 22 Mayan languages plus Garifuna and Xinka as national languages; they are not listed, so the owner should decide whether to include them. The color meanings (strength, justice, truth, loyalty; purity, integrity, firmness, light) are stated on Wikipedia without a decree number, so the flag text now says 'Officially' instead of 'By decree'. The Emblem of Guatemala article (Decree No. 33 of 1871, 1968 decree, 1997 spelling change) was not re-opened in the review pass. flagColors changed from Blue/White/Green to Blue/White/Blue to follow the hoist-to-fly band order; the arms also contain green and gold if the owner prefers to list them. Population came from Worldometers' copy of WPP 2024 because the UN data portal refused the request. Landmark pages were not opened individually.

flag.text: The blue, white and blue bands come from the flag of the Federal Republic of Central America, a union of five states. The flag dates from 1866; a 1949 law fixed its details. The five stars are those states and the hope that they will unite again. The blue bands are said to be the Pacific and the Caribbean, and the white the land between them and peace. The shade of blue has officially changed more than once, between turquoise and navy.

reasons.why: Wikipedia: the design was based on the flag of the former United Provinces of Central America (Federal Republic of Central America), which Honduras joined in 1823; the same Central American blue-white-blue motif is shared with Guatemala, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica.

Wikipedia: created 16 February 1866 by Legislative Decree No. 7 during the presidency of José María Medina; Legislative Decree No. 29 of 18 January 1949, under Juan Manuel Gálvez, established the current specifications (the draft's '26 January 1949' was corrected to 18 January per the article).

reasons.feature: Five blue stars in an X pattern
reasons.why: Wikipedia: the stars represent the five nations of the former Federal Republic of Central America (El Salvador, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, Guatemala) and the hope that the nations may form a union again; the 1949 decree fixes their layout as four stars in a rectangle with one in the center.

reasons.feature: Meaning of the blue and white
reasons.why: Wikipedia states, without attributing it to law, that the two outer bands represent the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea and also the blue sky and brotherhood, and the inner band the land between the ocean and the sea, the peace and prosperity of its people, and purity of thoughts. Not found in a decree text, so hedged as 'said to be'.

Wikipedia: the 1949 decree specified turquoise blue; a dark navy blue was standard practice for decades; President Xiomara Castro's government announced use of the turquoise shade on 4 January 2022; on 27 January 2026 the flag returned officially to the previously used navy blue, fulfilling a National Party campaign promise (El Heraldo reports the National Congress vote). The text is worded so it stays true whichever shade is in use.

entries.remainingDoubts: The supplied image /tmp/flagwork/out/hn.png shows the turquoise shade, but the Flag of Honduras article (re-checked in this pass) says the flag officially returned to navy blue on 27 January 2026; the owner should decide whether to ship navy artwork. I did not open the 2026 decree, so whether the 1949 decree wording was formally amended is unverified; the last sentence of the flag text was rewritten to be shade-neutral. The ocean/land/peace meanings are from Wikipedia, not from a decree text, so they are labeled traditional. The 1949 decree date was corrected from 26 to 18 January per Wikipedia. Population came from Worldometers' copy of WPP 2024 because the UN data portal refused the request.

flag.text: The three bands come from the flag of the Federal Republic of Central America, which Nicaragua once joined. It was adopted in 1908 and made law in 1971. The blue is often said to be the two oceans, the white the land between. By law the triangle means equality, the five volcanoes the union of the five Central American states, the rainbow peace and the red cap liberty. Sun rays are often read as a bright future; gold letters name the country.

reasons.why: Wikipedia: the flag is based on, and inspired by, the flag of the Federal Republic of Central America, with a blue and white triband and a coat of arms in the center; the same Central American blue-white-blue motif is shared with Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Costa Rica.
Wikipedia: first adopted on 11 September 1908 but not made official until 27 August 1971 (law on national symbols); no decree numbers are given on the flag page.

reasons.feature: Meaning of blue and white bands
reasons.why: The Flag of Nicaragua article gives no meaning for the bands themselves (confirmed in this pass); the popular reading that the blue bands are the Pacific and Caribbean and the white the land between is documented for the sister Honduran flag of the same federation design, so it is hedged as 'often said to be'.

The Coat of arms of Nicaragua article (per the draft; not re-opened) says the triangle signifies equality; the Flag article itself gives the triangle no meaning. The 1971 law on national symbols is the basis claimed, but its text was not opened.

reasons.feature: Five volcanoes rising from the water
reasons.why: Flag article: the five volcanoes represent the original five member states of the federation; the Coat of arms article words it as the union and brotherhood of the five Central American countries.

Coat of arms article: the rainbow signifies peace; the Flag article instead groups it with the sun rays as symbolic of a bright future. The text uses the peace meaning attributed to the arms description. Its violet band makes Nicaragua one of the few flags using purple.
Flag article: the Cap of Liberty represents national freedom; Coat of arms article: symbol of liberty.
Flag article: the rays of the sun and the rainbow are symbolic of the bright future to come; no legal meaning for the rays was found, so the text hedges it as 'often read as'.

reasons.feature: Gold inscription REPUBLICA DE NICARAGUA - AMERICA CENTRAL
reasons.why: Flag article: the arms used today contain the name of the state, Republica de Nicaragua (historical versions read Provincias Unidas del Centro de America); the lower text names the region, America Central.

entries.remainingDoubts: I did not open the 1971 law text, so the 'By law' meanings (triangle equality, rainbow peace, cap liberty, volcanoes union) rest on the Coat of arms of Nicaragua article cited by the draft, which was not re-opened in this pass; the Flag article gives the rainbow a different reading (bright future) and no meaning for the triangle or the bands. The meaning of the blue and white bands is hedged. Wikipedia notes a 30 January 2025 constitutional amendment adding the FSLN flag as an additional national symbol; the national flag itself is unchanged and the point is left out of the text for neutrality. Population came from Worldometers' copy of WPP 2024 because the UN data portal refused the request. Masaya Volcano and León Cathedral pages were not opened individually.

flag.text: María de la Ossa de Amador, wife of Panama's first president, sewed the flag in 1903 from a sketch by his son, and it flew that November as Panama separated from Colombia. A 1949 law gives its meaning: blue is the Conservative Party, red the Liberal Party, the two main parties of the day, and white the peace between them. The blue star stands for purity and honesty, the red star for authority and law. A 1925 law made it permanent.

reasons.feature: Overall design of four equal squares (white upper left, red upper right, blue lower left, white lower right)
reasons.why: Created on 1 November 1903 by María de la Ossa de Amador, wife of first president Manuel Amador Guerrero, from a sketch by his son Manuel Encarnación Amador; she and two relatives sewed three copies, which were flown in Panama City when Panama separated from Colombia on 3 November 1903. The original had blue in the upper left square; the squares were shifted after independence, once blue had become a party color, so the upper left is now white.
Law 34 of 15 December 1949 (the national-symbols law referred to in Constitution Article 6) states that blue represents the Conservative Party.
Law 34 of 1949 states that red represents the Liberal Party, the Conservatives' rival at the time of independence.
Law 34 of 1949 says white stands for peace and purity, read as the peace between the two parties.

reasons.feature: Blue five-pointed star in the upper-left white square
reasons.why: Per Law 34 of 1949 the blue star symbolizes the purity and honesty of the life of the country.

reasons.feature: Red five-pointed star in the lower-right white square
reasons.why: Per Law 34 of 1949 the red star represents authority and law in the country; together the two stars symbolize the new republic.

Law 64 of 1904 ratified the modified design; Law 48 of 25 March 1925 officially adopted the current flag; Law 34 of 15 December 1949 set its specifications and symbolism; Decree 337 of 22 December 2017 standardized the official shades.

Said to represent the purity of the patriots' cause (also described as the purity of their ideals).

flag.text: Alwin Bully designed the flag for independence in 1978; small changes came later. Officially, green stands for the lush forests, and the yellow, black and white cross for the Trinity and faith in God, its colors for the sun and first peoples, the dark soil and African roots, and clear rivers. The red disc stands for social justice, the ten green stars for the ten parishes, and the Sisserou parrot, found nowhere else, for aiming ever higher.

reasons.why: Designed by Dominican playwright Alwin Bully in early 1978 and adopted on 3 November 1978, the day of independence from Britain. Wikipedia says the design was modified in 1981, 1988 and 1990 and Britannica says three modifications with the latest on 3 November 1990, while the government's own description says it was modified in 1988; the flag text therefore says only that small changes came later.
The government says the forest green background symbolizes the island's rich, verdant forests and general lushness.

reasons.feature: Cross of three stripes: yellow, black and white
reasons.why: The government describes the three vertical and three horizontal stripes of yellow, black and white as a triple colored cross representing the Trinity of God, the cross itself showing belief in God since the state is founded on principles acknowledging the supremacy of God. Yellow stands for sunshine, the main crops (citrus and bananas) and the first inhabitants, the Carib and Arawak peoples; black for the rich black soil and African heritage; white for the clarity of rivers and waterfalls and the purity of the people's aspirations.
The government says the red central emblem symbolizes Dominica's commitment to social justice (Britannica phrases this as socialism, reflecting the politics of 1978).

reasons.feature: Ten green five-pointed stars (yellow-edged) around the disc
reasons.why: The government says the ten lime green stars, the traditional symbol of hope, represent the ten parishes of the country (St. Andrew, St. David, St. George, St. John, St. Joseph, St. Luke, St. Mark, St. Patrick, St. Paul and St. Peter), each with equal status, and so the equality of the people.

reasons.feature: Sisserou parrot (purple and green bird on a twig)
reasons.why: The government says the central emblem presents the national bird, the Sisserou parrot (Amazona imperialis, the imperial amazon), a symbol of flight toward greater heights and fulfilment of aspiration, and that the parrot also comes from the coat of arms and so stands for the official seal of the country. The bird lives only on Dominica and is critically endangered; its purple plumage makes this one of very few national flags containing purple.

flag.text: Juan Pablo Duarte's secret society La Trinitaria made the flag for the 1844 uprising against Haitian rule, keeping Haiti's blue and red but adding a white cross for Christian faith. Officially, blue stands for the sky and God's protection, red for the blood shed by the patriots, and white for peace and unity. The center carries the coat of arms: an open Bible, a cross, flags, laurel and palm branches, and the motto God, Fatherland, Liberty.

reasons.why: Designed by independence leader Juan Pablo Duarte and his secret society La Trinitaria; the Presidency's national symbols page says the Trinitarios approved the design on 16 July 1838, that the flag was first raised on 27 February 1844 at the start of the uprising that ended Haitian rule (the country had been under Haiti since 1822), and that the Constituent Congress adopted it officially on 6 November 1844 with the first constitution. The current constitution (Article 31) prescribes ultramarine blue and vermilion red in alternating quarters, blue at the top next to the pole, separated by a white cross half the height of a quarter, with the coat of arms at the center.
Taken from the blue and red flag of Haiti, which ruled the territory until 1844; the new flag kept those colors and added the cross to set the Dominican nation apart.
Added by Duarte's movement as a Christian symbol, expressing the faith of the independence movement and distinguishing the flag from Haiti's.

The Dominican Presidency's national symbols page (fetched directly) says ultramarine blue represents the sky that covers the homeland, that God protects the Dominican nation, and the Dominicans' ideals of progress; Wikipedia and FOTW give liberty.
The Presidency page says vermilion red represents the blood shed by the patriots in the battles to win the nation's independence.
The Presidency page says white represents peace and union among all Dominicans; other sources also read it as sacrifice or salvation.

Adopted 6 November 1844 and altered many times since; it makes this the only national flag to show a Bible.

flag.text: Tradition says in 1803 rebel leader Jean-Jacques Dessalines tore the white out of a French flag and Catherine Flon sewed the blue and red together. Blue is often said to stand for Haitians of African descent and red for those of mixed descent; the law gives no meaning. The white square holds the coat of arms fixed by the 1987 constitution: a palm tree topped by a liberty cap over cannons and flags, with the motto Unity Makes Strength.

reasons.why: Wikipedia: according to tradition, on May 18, 1803, at the Congress of Arcahaie, Dessalines ripped the white center out of a French flag, white being associated with the white Europeans, and asked his goddaughter Catherine Flon to sew the remaining bands together. Presented as tradition in the text.

Wikipedia and FOTW give the traditional reading: blue for the Black Africans and red for the mulattos (people of mixed descent). The 1987 constitution names blue and red as the national colors but assigns no meaning, so the text hedges with 'often said'.

reasons.feature: White square with the coat of arms
reasons.why: Article 3 of the 1987 constitution, as quoted by Wikipedia: two equal horizontal bands, blue on top and red underneath, with the coat of arms of the Republic in the center on a white square.

reasons.feature: Palm tree topped by a liberty cap
reasons.why: Article 3 names a palmette surmounted by the liberty cap; the cap is the traditional emblem of freedom from slavery.

reasons.feature: Cannons, flags and other weapons beneath the palm
reasons.why: Article 3 calls for a trophy of arms under the palms; sources describe it as cannons, flags, drums and other weapons, marking the fight for independence.

reasons.feature: Motto ribbon L'Union fait la Force
reasons.why: Article 3 sets the legend L'Union fait la Force (In Union there is Strength / Unity Makes Strength) on the arms. The text gives an English translation.

Wikipedia: from 1964 to 1986 the Duvalier governments used Dessalines' black and red design and even blackened the flags in the trophy; blue and red returned in 1986 and are prescribed by the constitution ratified March 29, 1987 (Wikipedia also records a formal re-adoption of the current version on 25 February 2012). Mentioned only through 'fixed by the 1987 constitution' for length.

entries.remainingDoubts: Driving side rests on WorldStandards only (Wikipedia list fetch truncated, infobox lacked the line). Population is WPP 2024 via Worldometers, not the UN portal directly. Government (JIS): gold represents the natural wealth of the country and the beauty of the sunlight.
Government (JIS): green signifies hope and agricultural resources. JIS sums the flag up as 'The sun shineth; the land is green; and the people are strong and creative.'

reasons.why: Added for official government use on 31 October 1900; the plain flag without arms is used by the merchant marine. Wikipedia: the condor stretching its wings symbolizes power, greatness and strength; Chimborazo and the Guayas river stand for the land; the steamboat Guayas, in service from 9 October 1841, was the first seaworthy steamship built in Ecuador and all of South America; the sun is surrounded by Aries, Taurus, Gemini and Cancer for March to July, the months of the 1845 Marcist Revolution; the fasces represent republican dignity, the laurel the republic's victories and the palm the martyrs of independence.

entries.remainingDoubts: The color meanings are widely repeated (Wikipedia, FOTW) but no law or government text giving them was opened, so they are presented as the usual reading rather than as official. Population taken from Worldometers' WPP 2024 table, not population.un.org directly. Cotopaxi and the Historic Center of Quito were not separately fetched.

officialName.note: Wikipedia infobox name.

funFact.value: Guyana's Kaieteur Falls drops about 226 meters in a single plunge, more than four times the height of Niagara Falls, deep in the rainforest.

flag.text: Guyana's Golden Arrowhead flag was adopted at independence from Britain on 26 May 1966. American flag scholar Whitney Smith designed it; Britain's College of Arms added the white and black edges and swapped his red and green areas. The government says green stands for farmland and forests, white for the many rivers, the golden arrow for mineral wealth, black for the endurance of the people, and red for the energy of building a new nation.

reasons.feature: Overall design (golden arrowhead with red triangle on green), adopted 1966
reasons.why: Designed by American vexillologist Whitney Smith (proposal 1962; the government fact page names him as designer) and adopted on 26 May 1966, the day of independence from the United Kingdom; nicknamed the Golden Arrowhead.

reasons.feature: White and black edges and the red/green arrangement
reasons.why: Smith's original had no borders and used red for the large area and green for the small triangle; the College of Arms in Britain reversed those colors and added white and black borders before adoption (Wikipedia and FOTW; the government fact page does not mention this).
Government fact page (Guyana Lands and Surveys Commission): green symbolizes the agricultural and forested nature of Guyana.
Government fact page: white symbolizes the many rivers and water potential of Guyana.
Government fact page: gold symbolizes the mineral wealth and its forward thrust.
Government fact page: black symbolizes the strength and endurance of the Guyanese people.
Government fact page: red symbolizes the zeal and dynamic task of nation building.

flag.text: Paraguay's red, white and blue bands were fixed by Congress in 1842 and are said to echo the French flag as a sign of independence and liberty. Red is often read as justice, white as peace and blue as freedom, though the law gives no meaning. The two sides differ: the front carries the national seal, a yellow star in a palm and olive wreath ringed by the country's name; the back shows a lion under a red cap with the motto Peace and Justice.

reasons.feature: Three horizontal bands red, white, blue
reasons.why: Congress adopted the red-white-blue design on 25 November 1842 (date confirmed in the English Wikipedia infobox); the first 1811 flag was plain blue with a star, and an 1812 design introduced the three colors. The current version dates from Decree No. 11,400 of 15 July 2013.

reasons.feature: Choice of red, white and blue
reasons.why: Wikipedia says the design was inspired by the colors of the French flag to signify independence and liberty (and notes the same three colors appear on the Dutch flag), but cites no primary document, so the text hedges with 'said to'.

reasons.feature: Color meanings (red justice, white peace, blue liberty)
reasons.why: Spanish Wikipedia gives this popular reading; the English article and the 2013 Decree No. 11,400 that defines the flag specify only the colors and give them no meaning, so the reading is hedged.
Wikipedia states it is the only national flag with a different design on each side: the national coat of arms on the front and the seal of the treasury on the back, both fixed by decree.

reasons.feature: Front emblem: yellow star in a green palm and olive wreath, ringed by the words REPUBLICA DEL PARAGUAY
reasons.why: This is the national coat of arms as defined by the 2013 decree, which simplified it toward its 19th-century form: the blue circle around the star was removed and the inscription changed from yellow on red to black on a colorless background. No meaning is given for the star, the branches or the inscription in the sources, so none is stated.

reasons.feature: Back emblem: lion, red cap on a staff, motto Paz y Justicia
reasons.why: This is the seal of the treasury; the motto means Peace and Justice. Wikipedia says the red Phrygian cap symbolizes courage, while the Phrygian cap is more generally known as a cap of liberty; because the sources differ, the text names the cap without assigning it a meaning.

entries.remainingDoubts: Population comes from Worldometers' reproduction of WPP 2024 rather than the UN portal itself. The ₲ symbol and the Palacio de los López landmark are from general knowledge, not a fetched page. Wikipedia reads the Phrygian cap as courage while it is traditionally the cap of liberty; the text avoids giving it a meaning. The French-flag inspiration is stated by Wikipedia without a cited primary source, so it is presented as traditional. Spanish Wikipedia's color meanings were taken from the draft and not re-opened in review.

funFact.value: The Inca built Machu Picchu high in the Andes around 1450; the Spanish never found it, and it became known to the world only after a 1911 expedition.
funFact.note: 149 characters. Built c. 1450 under Pachacuti; not found by the Spanish; Hiram Bingham's 1911 expedition made it internationally known (locals knew of it earlier, hence 'known to the world').

driveSide.note: Right-hand traffic; agrees with the seed.

flag.text: Peru's three upright bands of red, white and red come from General José de San Martín, who chose the colors in 1820 during the war of independence from Spain; Congress fixed the design in 1825. A popular tale that red and white flamingos near Pisco inspired him is treated by historians as legend. Red is traditionally said to stand for the blood shed for independence and white for peace, though the constitution gives the colors no meaning.

reasons.feature: Three vertical bands red, white, red
reasons.why: San Martín decreed Peru's first red and white flag in October 1820; after changes by Torre Tagle and Bolívar, Congress adopted the present vertical red-white-red design on 25 February 1825. Article 49 of the constitution defines the flag as three vertical stripes with the outer ones red and the middle one white.

reasons.feature: Origin of the red and white colors
reasons.why: The story that San Martín took the colors from red and white flamingos (parihuanas) near Pisco comes from writer Abraham Valdelomar; historians instead suggest he drew on the flags of the liberation army's home countries, so the flamingo tale is presented as legend.

Red is commonly said to represent the blood of those who died for independence and white purity and peace; Wikipedia calls this the usual reading, but Article 49 of the constitution describes the flag without assigning meanings and no law giving them was found, so it is hedged.

entries.remainingDoubts: Population is from Worldometers' copy of WPP 2024, not the UN portal. The S/ symbol was not separately fetched. Wikipedia labels the red-for-blood meaning as official, but no law or constitutional article giving it was found, so it is reported as traditional. The state flag with the coat of arms (distinguished since 1950) is omitted from the text for length; the supplied image is the plain civil flag.

officialName.note: Wikipedia infobox.

funFact.value: Suriname is the smallest country in South America and the only independent state outside Europe where Dutch is the official language.
funFact.note: 133 characters. Both statements are made in the Suriname article (smallest sovereign country in South America; only independent state outside Europe with Dutch as official language).

driveSide.note: Left-hand traffic; Suriname and Guyana are the only two left-driving countries in South America. Agrees with the seed.

flag.text: Suriname adopted this flag at independence from the Netherlands on 25 November 1975, after a design contest won by art teacher Jack Pinas. The independence decree explains it: green for the fertile land and hope, white for justice and freedom, red for progress and renewal, and the yellow star for the unity of the nation and a golden future. One star replaced the five stars of the 1959 flag, which stood for separate ethnic groups.

reasons.why: Legally adopted 25 November 1975, the day Suriname became independent from the Netherlands (confirmed on Wikipedia); the design by art teacher and graphic designer Jack Pinas won a national competition and some changes were made to it before adoption.

The Governor's decree of 25 November 1975 (Government Gazette No. 160), as translated on FOTW, says green symbolizes the fertility of Suriname and its many possibilities and the hopeful expectations of the new Suriname; Wikipedia summarizes it as the richness of the agricultural lands.
The same decree says white symbolizes justice and also depicts freedom, linking the green of the land with the red of renewal; Wikipedia summarizes it as freedom and independence.
Officially red stands for progress and renewal, and the love which leads to deeds; Wikipedia summarizes it as progress and hope.
Officially the star symbolizes the unity of the nation and the yellow the sacrifices made for independence, pointing toward a golden (bright) future; Wikipedia gives the same three ideas.

The 1959-1975 flag showed five colored stars (black for Africans, brown for Asian Indians, yellow for Javanese and Chinese, red for Amerindians, white for Europeans) joined by a black ellipse on white; it was criticized for stressing ethnic differences rather than national unity, so the new flag uses one star for the whole nation.

entries.remainingDoubts: Population is from Worldometers' copy of WPP 2024, not the UN portal. Area differs between Wikipedia's area list (163,820) and the Suriname infobox (165,940); the list figure is used. The official 1975 decree text was read in the draft stage through FOTW's English translation (Jos Poels/André van de Loo), not the Surinamese gazette itself, and FOTW was not re-opened in review; Wikipedia's summary of the color meanings is worded slightly differently (green: agricultural richness; white: freedom and independence; red: progress and hope) but describes the same decree.

funFact.value: Uruguay is the only South American country that lies entirely south of the Tropic of Capricorn, so none of it is in the tropics.
funFact.note: 128 characters. Stated in the Wikipedia Uruguay article; a permanent geographic fact.

driveSide.note: Seed leftHand=false; both sources agree on right-hand traffic (Uruguay switched from left to right in the 20th century). No source disagreed.

flag.text: Uruguay's nine white and blue bands stand for the nine departments the country had when it became independent in 1828. Blue and white come from Argentina's flag of 1812, under which the region first fought Spain. The gold sun with a face is the Sun of May, recalling the May 1810 uprising in Buenos Aires that began the region's break from Spain. The flag was adopted in 1828 with nineteen bands, and a law of 1830 cut them to nine.

reasons.feature: Nine horizontal bands (five white, four blue)
reasons.why: Represent the nine original departments of Uruguay at independence (Canelones, Cerro Largo, Colonia, Durazno, Maldonado, Montevideo, Paysandú, San José, Soriano). The decree of 18 December 1828 gave nineteen alternating stripes; the law of 11 July 1830 reduced the design to four blue and five white stripes because the many thin stripes were hard to see from a distance. Verified against the Flag of Uruguay article in this pass; the image shows exactly nine bands.

Inherited from the blue-white-blue flag created by Manuel Belgrano in 1812 for the United Provinces (Argentina), under which the region fought Spain; José Gervasio Artigas adapted it around 1815 for the League of the Free Peoples. No Uruguayan law assigns a meaning to the colors, and the Flag of Uruguay article states the exact shades are not defined by law.

reasons.feature: Golden Sun of May with a human face and 16 rays in the upper left corner
reasons.why: Named for the May Revolution of 25 May 1810 in Buenos Aires, which began the independence movement in the Río de la Plata; Britannica records that the sun breaking through during the public gathering that day was taken as a favorable omen. The decree of 18 February 1952 fixed the Uruguayan form: a radiant circle with a face surrounded by sixteen rays, alternating triangular (straight) and wavy. The image shows the sun with a face and alternating straight and wavy rays in the upper left white band.

Often said to depict the Inca sun god Inti, but the Sun of May article notes this reading lacks documentary support from the revolutionary period and was popularized by 20th-century historians, so it is kept out of the main text.

Design by Joaquín Suárez; adopted by decree of 18 December 1828 with nineteen alternating stripes; law of 11 July 1830 set the current nine stripes, still in force; decree of 18 February 1952 standardized the sun. Confirmed against the Flag of Uruguay article in this pass.

entries.remainingDoubts: No law gives the blue and white a meaning; popular readings (sky, peace) seen in blogs were not used. The Inca-sun link is unproven and kept as a traditional note only. Currency symbol presentation varies, so the ISO code was used. Colonia del Sacramento and Punta del Este were chosen from general knowledge, not an opened source. Population uses the UN WPP 2024 series (3.39 million), lower than the 2023 census count (3.50 million); the mid-2024 WPP figure itself was taken from Worldometers rather than from the UN site, but the WPP 2024 mid-2022 and mid-2023 rows on Wikipedia agree with it.

languages.note: Spanish is the official language nationwide, as the seed ownerRules require. The constitution also makes indigenous languages official for the indigenous peoples in their regions; these are regional and not listed.

currency.note: The bolívar (the bolívar digital, ISO 4217 code VED) is the sole legal tender; the Central Bank writes prices with the abbreviation 'Bs.'. US dollars circulate widely in practice but are not legal tender, so only one currency is listed.

landmarks.note: Angel Falls and Lake Maracaibo are named as significant features in the Venezuela article. Mount Roraima's summit plateau is mostly in Venezuela (the peak marks the tripoint with Brazil and Guyana) and the classic trek is from the Venezuelan side; it was chosen from general knowledge, not an opened source.

funFact.value: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, plunging about 979 meters from the flat-topped mountain Auyán-tepui.
funFact.note: 141 characters. The Venezuela article names Angel Falls as a major landmark; the 979 m height and tallest-waterfall status are long-established figures but were not re-verified in a dedicated source during this pass.

driveSide.note: Seed leftHand=false; the worldstandards list states Venezuela drives on the right. No source disagreed.

flag.text: Independence hero Francisco de Miranda flew the yellow, blue and red bands in 1806; Colombia and Ecuador, once joined with Venezuela in Gran Colombia, share the colors. Yellow is often said to mean riches, blue the sea and red blood shed for freedom, but no law says so. Seven stars, added in 1817, honor the provinces that declared independence in 1811. A 2006 law added an eighth for Guayana province, as Simón Bolívar had ordered in 1817.

reasons.feature: Three horizontal bands: yellow, blue, red
reasons.why: Designed by Francisco de Miranda and first flown on 12 March 1806 at Jacmel, Haiti, during his expedition to free Venezuela from Spain, then over Venezuelan soil at La Vela de Coro on 3 August 1806; adopted by the 1811 Congress. The horizontal arrangement dates to the original 1811 flag, with equal bands formalized in 1864 (Britannica dates Miranda's choice of the colors to 1801). Verified against the Flag of Venezuela article in this pass; the image shows three equal bands.

reasons.feature: Shared yellow-blue-red motif with Colombia and Ecuador
reasons.why: Miranda's colors became the flag of Gran Colombia (1819 to 1831), the union of today's Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador and Panama, so Colombia and Ecuador kept the same three colors.

reasons.feature: Meaning of yellow, blue and red
reasons.why: Popularly read as yellow for the land's wealth or gold, blue for the sea (the Caribbean, separating Venezuela from Spain) and red for blood shed in the fight for independence. The Flag of Venezuela article presents these as traditional symbolism and does not say that the 1954 or 2006 law assigns them; the Spanish Wikipedia article gives no legal meaning for the colors, and Britannica notes that several different explanations circulated, so this is presented as tradition.

reasons.feature: Seven of the eight white stars in an arc on the blue band
reasons.why: Stars were first decreed on 17 May 1817 (Pampatar) to represent the seven provinces that signed the Declaration of Independence of 5 July 1811: Caracas, Cumaná, Barcelona, Barinas, Margarita, Mérida and Trujillo. The number of stars varied during the 19th century before settling at seven. The provinces list was confirmed against the Flag of Venezuela article in this pass.

The Ley de Bandera Nacional, Himno Nacional y Escudo de Armas, approved by the National Assembly in March 2006 (the Flag of Venezuela article gives 12 March 2006 as the adoption date of the current flag), added an eighth star for the province of Guayana, carrying out Simón Bolívar's decree of 20 November 1817 at Angostura, which ordered one star added to the seven as the emblem of Guayana after that province joined the republic. Stated neutrally without attributing it to any political figure, per the seed ownerRules. The image shows eight white stars in an arc.

reasons.feature: Coat of arms (not on this civil flag)
reasons.why: The state flag carries the national coat of arms in the upper left corner; the civil flag shown in the app image omits it (confirmed by opening the image), so it is not described in the text.

entries.remainingDoubts: Total area differs between Wikipedia's area list (912,050 km2, used) and the Venezuela article (916,445 km2); the list row's footnote [z] could not be read. The exact 2006 date varies by source (Britannica 7 March; Wikipedia 9 March for the law's approval and 12 March for adoption); the flag text avoids a day. Britannica dates Miranda's colors to 1801 while Wikipedia gives the first flying as 1806; the text uses 1806. The 2006 law's own text was not opened, only summaries of it, so the claim that no law assigns the color meanings rests on Wikipedia and Britannica; the eldiario and expansion.mx pages were seen as search snippets, not opened in full. The mid-2024 WPP figure was taken from Worldometers rather than from the UN site, though the WPP 2024 rows on Wikipedia agree with it. The Angel Falls height in the fun fact and Mount Roraima as a landmark come from general knowledge, not a source opened in this pass.

criticApplied.reason: Spanish rests only on a Cabinet policy decision of 13 May 2026 that tells the Ministry of Education to make Spanish a core school subject; no statute or constitutional change makes it an official language, and the entry's own note admits none was found. The field rule asks for official or national languages only, and the batch already excludes languages with firmer legal status (Guatemala's 2003 Law of National Languages), so listing Spanish for Antigua is inconsistent and likely to confuse a learner. Keep English alone until a law exists.

No entry in the existing catalog repeats a color (Argentina is listed as Light Blue, White, Yellow, naming the sun's color once rather than repeating Light Blue). Blue, White, Blue breaks that convention; the green quetzal and laurel wreath are the arms' main color, matching how Argentina's emblem color is listed.
Same convention: the catalog never repeats a color in flagColors; the Honduran flag has only blue and white (the stars are blue).
Removes the repeated Blue and treats the gold-lettered coat of arms the same way El Salvador's entry does (Blue, White, Gold), so the two gold-ringed federation arms are handled alike.

criticApplied.value: The bands copy the flag of the Central American federation of 1823 and were readopted in 1912. Blue is usually read as the two oceans around Central America, white as peace. The coat of arms, ringed by the country's name in gold, has five volcanoes for the federation's five states, a red liberty cap, a rainbow, the independence date 15 September 1821, five flags, 14 laurel bunches for the 14 departments, and the motto God, Union, Liberty.
criticApplied.reason: The motto DIOS UNION LIBERTAD is a visible feature of the arms and is prescribed by the 1972 law (per the entry's own reasons), but the text never mentions it, while the Guatemala and Nicaragua texts do cover their scroll and lettering. Rewritten to 442 characters so the motto fits within the 450 limit; no other meaning changed.

criticApplied.value: Anthony C. George designed the flag, first raised at independence on 7 February 1974. The government says red is for courage and vitality, gold for wisdom and the sun, green for fertile land and farming. The seven gold stars stand for the seven parishes; the star in the red circle is said to mark either the capital or the sister islands Carriacou and Petite Martinique. The nutmeg pod on the left recalls Grenada's fame as the Isle of Spice.
criticApplied.reason: Date format inconsistency: GD, TT and JM use month-day-year (February 7, 1974) while the other 25 Americas texts and the existing catalog (49 day-month-year dates vs 2 month-day) write 27 February 1967, 10 July 1973 etc. Only the date is changed; 443 characters.

criticApplied.value: Adopted on 31 August 1962 at independence from Britain, the flag was picked by the Independence Committee and credited to artist Carlisle Chang. A white-edged black band runs from the upper left corner to the lower right on red. Officially red is the sun's warmth and the people's courage, white the surrounding sea and equality, and black the people's dedication and the land's wealth: fire, water and earth. The diagonal has no set meaning.
criticApplied.reason: Same date-format inconsistency (August 31, 1962 → 31 August 1962); only the date and its comma changed; 442 characters.

criticApplied.value: Jamaica first flew the flag at independence on 6 August 1962; a parliamentary committee chose the gold diagonal cross on green and black. At first it was read as hardships there are, but the land is green and the sun shineth. Since 1996 it officially means black for the people's strength and creativity, gold for natural wealth and sunshine, and green for hope and agriculture. It is the only national flag with no red, white or blue.
criticApplied.reason: Same date-format inconsistency (August 6, 1962 → 6 August 1962); only the date changed; 435 characters.

Every other entry in this batch and almost all of the catalog use the pattern 'Country-adjective Name (symbol)' (Peruvian Sol, Paraguayan Guaraní, Venezuelan Bolívar); the Wikipedia article title is 'Bolivian boliviano'. Also note Venezuela writes the same abbreviation as 'Bs.' with a period; 'Bs' without the period is the simpler form for both.

criticNotes: Mechanical checks passed for all 28 entries: flag texts are 418 to 445 characters, fun facts 93 to 155 characters, no double quotes, line breaks, flag jargon or British spellings (the only hit, 'English Harbour' in the Antigua fun fact, is a proper place name). No two entries share a quizCapital (Kingston/Kingstown and St. John's/St. George's are distinct). Population roundings all follow the 3-significant-figure rule and none ends in 5 followed by zeros.
